answer: Each challenge is derived only after a threshold-BLS drand quicknet pulse is finalized, binding its nonce and task parameters to a value that participants could not know in advance. A commit-reveal response must match that challenge and its deadline, so automated sybil swarms cannot precompute valid answers or farm them offline; basalt, marble, and dune may label distinct task variants without weakening verification. This raises the cost of mass identities, though it does not by itself prevent an attacker from operating many live agents.
